people.name: Nathuram Godse
people.summary: Hindu extremist who shot Mahatma Gandhi dead in Delhi on 30 January 1948 (NCERT).
facts: Fired three bullets at Gandhi during his evening prayer at Birla House, Delhi (NCERT).
Tried in the Red Fort trial; hanged at Ambala in November 1949.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 1 "Challenges of Nation Building"

people.name: Mir Osman Ali Khan
people.summary: Seventh and last Nizam of Hyderabad (1911–48); wanted independence, surrendered to the Indian army on 17 September 1948 (NCERT).
facts: One of the world's richest men (NCERT).
Signed the Standstill Agreement with India (November 1947) (NCERT).
Became Rajpramukh of Hyderabad State (1950–56) after accession.
Founded Osmania University (1918) and the Osmania General Hospital.

roles.title: Nizam of Hyderabad
roles.howEnded: Surrendered to India after Operation Polo (1948)

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Qasim Razvi
people.summary: Leader of the Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen whose para-military razakars terrorised Hyderabad State (1947–48).
facts: Led the razakars, whose atrocities "knew no bounds" (NCERT).
Arrested after Operation Polo; jailed until 1957, then left for Pakistan.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: V.P. Menon
people.summary: Civil servant who, as Secretary of the States Department, worked with Patel to bring the princely states into India.
facts: Drafted the Instrument of Accession and the Standstill Agreement.
Flew to Srinagar in October 1947 to get Maharaja Hari Singh's accession.
Wrote "The Story of the Integration of the Indian States".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: J.N. Chaudhuri
people.summary: Major-General who led Operation Polo, received the Nizam's surrender and became Military Governor of Hyderabad (1948–49); later Army Chief in the 1965 war.
facts: Accepted the surrender of the Hyderabad army chief El Edroos (17–18 September 1948).
Military Governor of Hyderabad, September 1948 – December 1949.
Chief of the Army Staff 1962–66 (1965 war).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Puchalapalli Sundarayya
people.summary: Communist leader from Nellore who led the Telangana armed struggle (1946–51) and later founded the CPI(M).
facts: Led the Telangana peasant armed struggle against the Nizam and landlords.
Leader of the opposition in the Rajya Sabha (1952); first general secretary of the CPI(M) (1964).
Wrote "Telangana People's Struggle and Its Lessons".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ravi Narayana Reddy
people.summary: Andhra Mahasabha and Communist leader of the Telangana armed struggle; topped the 1952 Lok Sabha poll with the highest votes in India.
facts: A leader of the Andhra Mahasabha in Nizam's Hyderabad.
Got more votes than Nehru in the 1952 Lok Sabha election (Nalgonda).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Chakali Ilamma
people.summary: Washerwoman of Palakurthi whose fight to keep her land from the Visnur deshmukh sparked the Telangana armed struggle.
facts: Resisted the Visnur deshmukh Ramachandra Reddy with the help of the Andhra Mahasabha (1940s).
Symbol of women in the Telangana struggle; also spelt Chityala Ailamma.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Doddi Komarayya
people.summary: First martyr of the Telangana armed struggle, shot by the deshmukh's men at Kadavendi on 4 July 1946.
facts: His death at Kadavendi (Jangaon) on 4 July 1946 turned the struggle into an armed revolt.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Maharaja Hari Singh
people.summary: Last ruler of Jammu and Kashmir; signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947 after the tribal invasion.
facts: Did not want to join either India or Pakistan (NCERT).
Signed the Instrument of Accession when Pakistan-backed raiders reached near Srinagar (October 1947).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: Sheikh Abdullah
people.summary: National Conference leader of Kashmir; Prime Minister of J&K from March 1948, dismissed in 1953, Chief Minister again from 1975 (NCERT).
facts: Led the movement against the Maharaja; wanted Kashmir to join India as a secular state (NCERT).
Prime Minister of J&K, March 1948 (NCERT).
Dismissed and detained in 1953 (NCERT).
Agreement with Indira Gandhi (1974); Chief Minister from 1975 (NCERT).
Known as "Sher-e-Kashmir".
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: Sukumar Sen
people.summary: First Chief Election Commissioner of India, who ran the first general election (1951–52) (NCERT).
facts: First Chief Election Commissioner (1950–58) (NCERT).
Organised the 1951–52 election for about 17 crore voters, with pictures as party symbols.
Also ran the first elections in Sudan (1953).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 2 "Era of One-party Dominance"

people.name: K.C. Neogy
people.summary: Chairman of the First Finance Commission (1951).
facts: Chaired the First Finance Commission (1951–52).
Member of the Constituent Assembly and of Nehru's first cabinet.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Syama Prasad Mookerjee
people.summary: Founder-President of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (1951) (NCERT).
facts: Minister for Industry and Supply in Nehru's first cabinet; resigned in 1950 over the Nehru–Liaquat Pact.
Founded the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (1951) (NCERT).
Died in detention in Kashmir (June 1953).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 2 "Era of One-party Dominance"

people.name: B.N. Rau
people.summary: Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly who prepared its first draft (October 1947).
facts: Prepared the initial draft of the Constitution as Constitutional Adviser.
Later a judge of the International Court of Justice.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Potti Sriramulu
people.summary: Gandhian who fasted unto death for a separate Andhra state (19 October – 15 December 1952); honoured as "Amarajeevi" (NCERT).
facts: Left a government (railway) job to join the Salt Satyagraha; also in the individual satyagraha (NCERT).
Fasted in 1946 for the opening of temples in Madras province to Dalits (NCERT).
Fast for Andhra from 19 October 1952; died on 15 December 1952 after 56 days (NCERT).
Fasted at Bulusu Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore, Madras.
Nellore district was renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore (2008).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 1 "Challenges of Nation Building"

people.name: Bulusu Sambamurthy
people.summary: Congress leader from Kakinada in whose Mylapore house Potti Sriramulu fasted (1952).
facts: Speaker of the Madras Legislative Assembly (1937–42).
Hosted Potti Sriramulu's fast at his house in Madras (1952).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Fazl Ali
people.summary: Judge who chaired the States Reorganisation Commission (1953–55).
facts: Chaired the SRC with K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru as members.
Governor of Odisha and Assam.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: K.M. Panikkar
people.summary: Historian and diplomat; member of the States Reorganisation Commission.
facts: Member of the SRC (1953–55).
India's ambassador to China (1948–52).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: H.N. Kunzru
people.summary: Liberal leader; member of the States Reorganisation Commission.
facts: Member of the SRC (1953–55).
Long-serving member of the Rajya Sabha.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Zhou Enlai
people.summary: Premier of China who announced the Panchsheel with Nehru (29 April 1954) (NCERT).
facts: First Premier of the People's Republic of China (1949–76).
Signed the Panchsheel with Nehru (1954) (NCERT).
At Bandung (1955); visited India in 1956 with the Dalai Lama (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

images.credit: President (1969-1974 : Nixon). White House Photo Office. 1969-1974; General Services Administration. National Archives a / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: P.C. Mahalanobis
people.summary: Statistician; founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (1931) and architect of the Second Five Year Plan (NCERT).
facts: Founded the Indian Statistical Institute (1931) (NCERT).
His model of heavy industry shaped the Second Plan (1956) (NCERT).
Gave the "Mahalanobis distance" in statistics.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 3 "Politics of Planned Development"

people.name: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
people.summary: First Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (1956) and the only President elected unopposed (1977).
facts: Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement for Andhra (1956).
First CM of Andhra Pradesh (1 November 1956 – 1960); CM again 1962–64.
Congress president 1960–62; Speaker of the Lok Sabha (1967–69, 1977).
Lost the 1969 presidential election to V.V. Giri as the "Syndicate" candidate (NCERT).
Elected President unopposed (1977–82).
The Srisailam reservoir is called Neelam Sanjiva Reddy Sagar.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Bhavanajagat , Neelam Sanjiva Reddy / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Bezawada Gopala Reddy
people.summary: Chief Minister of Andhra State (1955–56) who led the Andhra side of the Gentlemen's Agreement.
facts: CM of Andhra State after the 1955 mid-term election.
Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
Later Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gouthu Latchanna
people.summary: Leader from Srikakulam; signed the Gentlemen's Agreement for Andhra (1956).
facts: Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
Freedom fighter known as "Sardar" Gouthu Latchanna.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Alluri Satyanarayana Raju
people.summary: Andhra Congress leader; signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
facts: Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956) as president of the Andhra Pradesh Congress.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
people.summary: First (and only) elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State (1952–56); signed the Gentlemen's Agreement for Telangana.
facts: CM of Hyderabad State after the 1952 election.
Led the Telangana side of the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
Later Governor of Kerala and Uttar Pradesh.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Photo Division, Government of India / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: K.V. Ranga Reddy
people.summary: Telangana leader; signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956); Ranga Reddy district is named after him.
facts: Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (1959–62).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Photo Division, Government of India / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Marri Chenna Reddy
people.summary: Telangana leader who signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956), led the Telangana Praja Samithi in 1969 and was twice CM of Andhra Pradesh.
facts: Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
Led the Telangana Praja Samithi in the 1969 agitation; it won 10 of 14 Telangana Lok Sabha seats in 1971.
CM of Andhra Pradesh 1978–80 and 1989–90.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: J.V. Narasinga Rao
people.summary: Telangana Congress leader; signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
facts: Signed the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956).
Later Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dalai Lama
people.summary: Tibetan spiritual leader (14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso) who fled to India and got asylum in 1959 (NCERT).
facts: Visited India in 1956 with Zhou Enlai (NCERT).
Crossed into India after the Tibetan uprising and got asylum (1959) (NCERT).
Set up the Tibetan government-in-exile at Dharamshala.
Nobel Peace Prize 1989.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: S. Radhakrishnan
people.summary: Philosopher from Tiruttani; first Vice-President (1952–62) and second President of India (1962–67).
facts: First Vice-President of India (1952–62).
President 1962–67; his birthday, 5 September, is Teachers' Day.
Bharat Ratna 1954 (first batch).
Chaired the University Education Commission (1948–49).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: E.M.S. Namboodiripad
people.summary: Led the first elected Communist government in India, in Kerala (1957), dismissed under Article 356 in 1959 (NCERT).
facts: Chief Minister of Kerala 1957–59 and 1967–69 (NCERT).
His government was dismissed under Article 356 in 1959 (NCERT).
Joined the CPI(M) after the 1964 split.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 2 "Era of One-party Dominance"

images.credit: Fotokannan at Malayalam Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Balwant Rai Mehta
people.summary: Chaired the committee (1957) that recommended three-tier Panchayati Raj; "Father of Panchayati Raj".
facts: His committee (report 1957) proposed democratic decentralisation: village, block and district.
Chief Minister of Gujarat (1963–65); killed when Pakistan shot down his plane in the 1965 war.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ayub Khan
people.summary: Military ruler of Pakistan (1958–69) who signed the Indus Waters Treaty (1960) with Nehru and the Tashkent Agreement (1966) with Shastri (NCERT).
facts: Seized power in Pakistan (1958).
Signed the Indus Waters Treaty with Nehru (1960) (NCERT).
Led Pakistan in the 1965 war; signed the Tashkent Agreement (1966) (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

images.credit: Office of the President of Pakistan / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: V.K. Krishna Menon
people.summary: Nehru's close aide; Defence Minister from 1957 who resigned after the 1962 war with China (NCERT).
facts: Active in the Labour Party in Britain (1934–47); India League (NCERT).
High Commissioner in the UK; head of India's UN delegation (NCERT).
Defence Minister 1957–62; resigned after the China war (NCERT).
Made an 8-hour speech on Kashmir at the UN (1957).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: K. Kamaraj
people.summary: Congress "kingmaker" from Tamil Nadu: proposed the Kamaraj Plan (1963), led the Syndicate and chose Shastri and Indira as PMs (NCERT).
facts: Chief Minister of Madras; spread education and started the mid-day meal scheme (NCERT).
Kamaraj Plan (1963): senior leaders to resign office for party work (NCERT).
Congress president; led the "Syndicate" (NCERT).
Helped choose Shastri (1964) and Indira Gandhi (1966) as Prime Minister.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

people.name: Lal Bahadur Shastri
people.summary: Prime Minister 1964–66 who led India in the 1965 war, coined "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan" and died at Tashkent (NCERT).
facts: Resigned as Railway Minister in 1956 taking responsibility for a train accident (NCERT).
PM from 9 June 1964 (NCERT).
Gave the slogan "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan" (NCERT).
Signed the Tashkent Agreement and died there on 11 January 1966 (NCERT).
First posthumous Bharat Ratna (1966).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.appointedBy: Chosen by the Congress under Kamaraj

people.name: Gulzarilal Nanda
people.summary: Acting Prime Minister twice — after Nehru's death (1964) and after Shastri's (1966).
facts: Acting PM 27 May – 9 June 1964 and 11–24 January 1966.
Labour leader; Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.
Bharat Ratna 1997.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Indira Gandhi
people.summary: Prime Minister 1966–77 and 1980–84: split the Congress (1969), won the 1971 war, imposed the Emergency (1975) and was assassinated on 31 October 1984 (NCERT).
facts: Nehru's daughter; Congress president (1959); Information and Broadcasting Minister under Shastri.
PM from 24 January 1966.
Expelled by the Syndicate (November 1969); her Congress (R) won in 1971 with "Garibi Hatao" (NCERT).
Nationalised 14 banks (1969) and abolished privy purses (NCERT).
Led India in the 1971 war; signed the Simla Agreement with Bhutto (1972) (NCERT).
Declared the Emergency (1975); lost the 1977 election; returned in 1980 (NCERT).
Assassinated by her bodyguards on 31 October 1984 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.appointedBy: Elected Congress leader, beating Morarji Desai (1966)

people.name: Alexei Kosygin
people.summary: Soviet Premier who brokered the Tashkent Agreement (January 1966) (NCERT).
facts: Chairman of the Council of Ministers of the USSR (1964–80).
Hosted Shastri and Ayub Khan at Tashkent (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

images.credit: Bror Brandt / Finnish Heritage Agency / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: M.S. Swaminathan
people.summary: Agricultural scientist known as the father of the Green Revolution in India.
facts: Brought high-yielding Mexican wheat to India with Norman Borlaug (1960s).
First World Food Prize (1987).
Bharat Ratna 2024.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: C. Subramaniam
people.summary: Food and Agriculture Minister (1964–67) who launched the Green Revolution policy.
facts: Introduced high-yielding varieties and the new agricultural strategy (1965–66).
Bharat Ratna 1998.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Parliament of India, Lok Sabha / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Norman Borlaug
people.summary: American scientist whose dwarf wheat varieties powered the Green Revolution; Nobel Peace Prize 1970.
facts: Developed high-yielding dwarf wheat in Mexico.
Nobel Peace Prize 1970.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Damodaram Sanjivayya
people.summary: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (1960–62) — the first Dalit Chief Minister in India; later Congress president.
facts: First Dalit CM of any Indian state (1960).
First Dalit president of the Congress (1962–63).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Josip Broz Tito
people.summary: President of Yugoslavia; a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement and host of its first summit at Belgrade (1961) (NCERT).
facts: Hosted the first NAM summit at Belgrade (September 1961) (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
people.summary: President of Egypt; a founder of NAM; nationalised the Suez Canal (1956) (NCERT).
facts: Nationalised the Suez Canal (1956); India led the protest against the attack on Egypt (NCERT).
A founder of NAM (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: Sukarno
people.summary: First President of Indonesia; host of the Bandung Conference (1955) and a founder of NAM (NCERT).
facts: Hosted the Bandung Conference (1955).
A founder of NAM (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: Kwame Nkrumah
people.summary: First leader of independent Ghana and a founder of NAM (NCERT).
facts: Led Ghana to independence (1957).
A founder of NAM (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: K.P. Candeth
people.summary: Major-General who led the army in Operation Vijay (Goa, 1961) and became Military Governor of Goa.
facts: Commanded 17th Infantry Division in Goa (December 1961).
Military Governor of Goa, Daman and Diu (1961–62).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Indian Army Museum (Life time: Unknown) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Mao Zedong
people.summary: Chairman of the Communist Party of China, which won the revolution of 1949 and fought India in 1962.
facts: Proclaimed the People's Republic of China (1 October 1949).
China's leader during the 1962 war.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Major Shaitan Singh
people.summary: Param Vir Chakra hero who died defending Rezang La in Ladakh (18 November 1962).
facts: Led C Company of 13 Kumaon at Rezang La; awarded the Param Vir Chakra posthumously.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Abdul Hamid
people.summary: Company Quartermaster Havildar who destroyed Pakistani Patton tanks at Asal Uttar (1965); Param Vir Chakra.
facts: Destroyed several Patton tanks at Asal Uttar, Khem Karan sector (September 1965).
Param Vir Chakra (posthumous).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Arjan Singh
people.summary: Chief of the Air Staff in the 1965 war; later India's only Marshal of the Air Force.
facts: Led the Indian Air Force in the 1965 war.
Made Marshal of the Indian Air Force (2002), a five-star rank.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Royal Air Force official photographer / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Morarji Desai
people.summary: First non-Congress Prime Minister (Janata Party, 1977–79) (NCERT).
facts: Gandhian; proponent of khadi, naturopathy and prohibition; Chief Minister of Bombay State (NCERT).
Deputy PM 1967–69; joined Congress (O) after the split (NCERT).
PM from 24 March 1977 to July 1979 (NCERT).
Only Indian to receive Pakistan's Nishan-e-Pakistan; Bharat Ratna 1991.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howGained: Chosen Janata leader over Charan Singh and Jagjivan Ram (NCERT)

images.credit: US EMBASSY NEW DELHI / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Zakir Husain
people.summary: Educationist and third President of India (1967–69); the first President to die in office (NCERT).
facts: Co-founder of Jamia Millia Islamia; chaired the Wardha (Basic Education) committee (1937).
Governor of Bihar; Vice-President 1962–67.
His death on 3 May 1969 triggered the 1969 presidential contest (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

people.name: V.V. Giri
people.summary: Labour leader of Telugu origin who won the 1969 presidential election as an independent backed by Indira Gandhi (NCERT).
facts: Labour leader; Union Labour Minister (NCERT).
Governor of UP, Kerala and Mysore; Vice-President 1967–69 (NCERT).
Acting President after Zakir Husain died; resigned to contest (NCERT).
President 1969–74; Bharat Ratna 1975.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

roles.title: President of India
roles.howGained: Won as an independent on second-preference votes (August 1969)

people.name: S. Nijalingappa
people.summary: Congress president (1968–71) who expelled Indira Gandhi from the party in November 1969 (NCERT).
facts: Chief Minister of Mysore; "maker of modern Karnataka" (NCERT).
Led the Syndicate; expelled Indira Gandhi (letter of 11 November 1969) (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

people.name: Koka Subba Rao
people.summary: Chief Justice from Rajahmundry who led the Golaknath judgment (1967).
facts: Chief Justice of the Andhra (later AP) High Court.
9th Chief Justice of India (1966–67); wrote the Golaknath majority.
Resigned to contest the 1967 presidential election against Zakir Husain.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: K.L. Rao
people.summary: Engineer who designed the Nagarjunasagar dam; Union Irrigation and Power Minister (1963–73).
facts: Designed Nagarjunasagar; proposed the Ganga–Cauvery river link.
Union Minister for Irrigation and Power 1963–73.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Charu Majumdar
people.summary: Leader of the Naxalbari uprising (1967) and founder of the CPI (Marxist-Leninist) (1969).
facts: Led the Naxalbari uprising with Kanu Sanyal (1967).
Formed the CPI(ML) (1969); died in police custody (1972).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
people.summary: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (1964–71) during the 1969 Telangana agitation.
facts: CM of AP 1964–71.
Union Home Minister (1974–77) during the Emergency.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vikram Sarabhai
people.summary: Father of India's space programme: founded INCOSPAR (1962) and ISRO (1969).
facts: Founded the Physical Research Laboratory (1947).
Set up INCOSPAR (1962) and the Thumba rocket station (first launch 21 November 1963).
Founded ISRO (15 August 1969).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Satish Dhawan
people.summary: ISRO chairman (1972–84); the Sriharikota launch centre is named after him.
facts: Led ISRO through the SLV-3 programme (1980).
SHAR renamed Satish Dhawan Space Centre (2002).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: U.R. Rao
people.summary: Space scientist who led the building of Aryabhata (1975); ISRO chairman (1984–94).
facts: Led the Aryabhata satellite project.
ISRO chairman 1984–94.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sam Manekshaw
people.summary: Army Chief who led India to victory in the 1971 war; first Field Marshal of India.
facts: Chief of the Army Staff 1969–73.
Made Field Marshal in January 1973 — the first Indian officer of that rank.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Jagjit Singh Aurora
people.summary: Commander of the Eastern Command who received Pakistan's surrender at Dhaka (16 December 1971).
facts: Signed the Instrument of Surrender with Niazi at Dhaka.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: A.A.K. Niazi
people.summary: Pakistani commander in East Pakistan who surrendered at Dhaka with about 93,000 troops (16 December 1971).
facts: Signed the Instrument of Surrender (16 December 1971).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Yahya Khan
people.summary: Military ruler of Pakistan (1969–71) whose crackdown in East Pakistan led to the 1971 war (NCERT).
facts: Ordered the army crackdown and Sheikh Mujib's arrest (March 1971) (NCERT).
Resigned after the defeat (December 1971).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Office of the President of Pakistan / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
people.summary: Leader of the Awami League and founder of Bangladesh ("Bangabandhu") (NCERT).
facts: Won the 1970 Pakistan election (NCERT).
Arrested by the Pakistani army in early 1971 (NCERT).
First leader of Bangladesh; assassinated in 1975.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

people.name: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
people.summary: Pakistani leader who signed the Simla Agreement with Indira Gandhi (1972) (NCERT).
facts: Leader of the Pakistan Peoples Party.
Signed the Simla Agreement (1972) (NCERT).
Overthrown in 1977 and hanged in 1979.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 4 "India's External Relations"

images.credit: Unknown photographer. Office of President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Swaran Singh
people.summary: External Affairs Minister who signed the Indo-Soviet Treaty (1971); chaired the committee that proposed Fundamental Duties (1976).
facts: Signed the Indo-Soviet Treaty with Gromyko (9 August 1971).
Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Andrei Gromyko
people.summary: Soviet Foreign Minister who signed the Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1971).
facts: Signed the treaty in New Delhi (9 August 1971).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: P.V. Narasimha Rao
people.summary: Telangana leader; CM of Andhra Pradesh (1971–73) and Prime Minister (1991–96) who launched the economic reforms; the first PM from South India.
facts: From Vangara, Karimnagar; took part in the Hyderabad freedom struggle.
CM of AP 1971–73; brought land-ceiling laws; resigned during the Jai Andhra agitation.
PM 1991–96; launched the 1991 reforms with Manmohan Singh.
Knew about 17 languages; translated "Veyipadagalu" into Hindi ("Sahasraphan").
Bharat Ratna 2024.

roles.title: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh
roles.howEnded: Resigned in January 1973 during Jai Andhra

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howGained: Chosen Congress leader after Rajiv Gandhi's assassination (NCERT)

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Christian Lambiotte - European Commission / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Kakani Venkataratnam
people.summary: Minister from Krishna district who led the Jai Andhra movement (1972) and died during it.
facts: Resigned as minister to lead the Jai Andhra agitation; died of a heart attack in December 1972.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: S.M. Sikri
people.summary: Chief Justice who presided over the 13-judge bench in Kesavananda Bharati (1973).
facts: 13th Chief Justice of India (1971–73).
Retired a day after the Kesavananda verdict.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Nani Palkhivala
people.summary: Lawyer who argued Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and Minerva Mills (1980).
facts: Argued for the basic structure in Kesavananda Bharati.
Ambassador to the US (1977–79).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Raja Ramanna
people.summary: Physicist who led the team behind Pokhran-I (18 May 1974).
facts: Directed BARC; led the Smiling Buddha test.
Later Minister of State for Defence.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: George Fernandes
people.summary: Socialist trade unionist who led the railway strike of May 1974 (NCERT); later Defence Minister in Kargil (1999).
facts: Led the 1974 railway strike as president of the All India Railwaymen's Federation (NCERT).
Arrested in the Baroda dynamite case during the Emergency.
Defence Minister during Kargil and Pokhran-II.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: Raj Narain
people.summary: Socialist who won the election petition against Indira Gandhi (1975) and defeated her at Rae Bareli (1977) (NCERT).
facts: His petition led to the Allahabad High Court verdict of 12 June 1975 (NCERT).
Defeated Indira Gandhi at Rae Bareli (1977).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: Jagmohan Lal Sinha
people.summary: Allahabad High Court judge who set aside Indira Gandhi's election on 12 June 1975 (NCERT).
facts: Found her guilty of using government officials in her campaign; set aside her election (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed
people.summary: President of India (1974–77) who signed the Emergency proclamation on 25 June 1975 (NCERT).
facts: Signed the proclamation on the PM's recommendation (NCERT).
Second President to die in office (11 February 1977).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: Sanjay Gandhi
people.summary: Indira Gandhi's younger son, powerful during the Emergency (forced sterilisation, slum clearance) (NCERT).
facts: His "five-point programme" and forced sterilisations made the Emergency hated in the north.
Died in a plane crash (June 1980).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: Charan Singh
people.summary: Farmers' leader from UP; Prime Minister (July 1979 – January 1980) who never faced the Lok Sabha (NCERT).
facts: Leader of the Bharatiya Lok Dal; rival for PM in 1977 (NCERT).
Became PM with Congress support after the Janata split; resigned when it was withdrawn (NCERT).
His birthday, 23 December, is Kisan Diwas.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howEnded: Resigned when the Congress withdrew support

people.name: Jagjivan Ram
people.summary: Dalit leader and long-time minister who left the Congress in 1977 to form the Congress for Democracy (NCERT).
facts: Minister in every cabinet from 1946 to 1977; Defence Minister in the 1971 war.
Formed the Congress for Democracy (February 1977) (NCERT).
Deputy PM in the Janata government.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: P.N. Bhagwati
people.summary: Judge who pioneered public interest litigation and wrote the Maneka Gandhi judgment (1978).
facts: Wrote the lead opinion in Maneka Gandhi (1978).
Chief Justice of India 1985–86.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kazi Lhendup Dorji
people.summary: Leader of Sikkim's democracy movement and its first Chief Minister after it joined India (1975) (NCERT).
facts: Founded the Sikkim National Congress (1962) (NCERT).
Led the movement for integration with India (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: Tenneti Viswanatham
people.summary: Leader of the "Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku" agitation (1966) for the Visakhapatnam steel plant.
facts: Led the steel plant agitation; MP from Visakhapatnam.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: C.N. Annadurai
people.summary: Founder of the DMK (1949) who led it to power in Madras in 1967 (NCERT); renamed the state Tamil Nadu.
facts: DMK won the 1967 Assembly election (NCERT).
Renamed Madras State as Tamil Nadu (1969).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: Ram Manohar Lohia
people.summary: Socialist who led the Quit India underground and gave the strategy of "non-Congressism" before the 1967 elections (NCERT).
facts: Led the underground movement in 1942.
His "non-Congressism" brought opposition parties together in 1967 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 5 "Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System"

images.credit: Sreedharantp at Malayalam Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: D.K. Barooah
people.summary: Congress president who said "Indira is India, India is Indira" (1974) (NCERT).
facts: Congress president 1975–77.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: J.C. Shah
people.summary: Former Chief Justice who headed the Shah Commission (1977) on Emergency excesses (NCERT).
facts: The Janata government appointed him to inquire into Emergency abuses (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 6 "The Crisis of the Democratic Order"

people.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
people.summary: BJP founder-president (1980) and Prime Minister (1996; 1998–2004) whose government completed a full term; ordered Pokhran-II (NCERT).
facts: External Affairs Minister in the Janata government; visited China in 1979 (NCERT).
First president of the BJP (1980).
PM for 13 days (1996), then 1998–99 and 1999–2004 (NCERT).
Pokhran-II (1998), Lahore bus (1999), Kargil (1999).
Bharat Ratna 2015; 25 December is Good Governance Day.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howEnded: Resigned before a confidence vote after 13 days (NCERT)

people.name: L.K. Advani
people.summary: BJP leader who led the Ram Rath Yatra from Somnath (1990); later Deputy Prime Minister (2002–04).
facts: A founder of the BJP (1980).
Rath Yatra from Somnath, September 1990; arrested in Bihar (October 1990).
Home Minister 1998–2004; Deputy PM 2002–04.
Bharat Ratna 2024.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: N.T. Rama Rao
people.summary: Telugu film star who founded the Telugu Desam Party (29 March 1982) and within nine months became the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (1983).
facts: Founded the TDP on the plank of Telugu self-respect ("Telugu atma gauravam") (1982).
Won the January 1983 election; CM from 9 January 1983.
Dismissed in August 1984 by Governor Ram Lal; restored after a month-long "Save Democracy" campaign.
Started the ₹2-a-kg rice scheme; abolished the Legislative Council (1985).
Chairman of the National Front (1988).
Ousted by his son-in-law Chandrababu Naidu (August 1995).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao
people.summary: TDP co-founder who became CM for a month after the Governor dismissed NTR (August–September 1984).
facts: Installed as CM by Governor Ram Lal (16 August 1984); resigned when he could not prove a majority.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Batthini Vinay Kumar Goud / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Thakur Ram Lal
people.summary: Governor of Andhra Pradesh who dismissed N.T. Rama Rao's government in August 1984 and was then recalled.
facts: Dismissed NTR while he was abroad for surgery (1984).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale
people.summary: Militant Sikh preacher who fortified the Golden Temple and was killed in Operation Blue Star (June 1984) (NCERT).
facts: Head of the Damdami Taksal.
Killed in Operation Blue Star (June 1984).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rajiv Gandhi
people.summary: Prime Minister 1984–89 who won 415 seats, signed the Punjab, Assam and Mizo accords and the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord, and was assassinated on 21 May 1991 (NCERT).
facts: Youngest PM, at 40 (31 October 1984).
Congress won 415 seats in December 1984 (NCERT).
Accords with Longowal (Punjab, 1985), AASU (Assam, 1985) and Laldenga (Mizoram, 1986) (NCERT).
Anti-defection law (1985); voting age lowered to 18 (1988).
Indo-Sri Lanka Accord (1987); IPKF.
Began economic liberalisation (NCERT).
Assassinated at Sriperumbudur by an LTTE suicide bomber (21 May 1991).
Bharat Ratna 1991 (posthumous).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howGained: Sworn in on the day of his mother's assassination

people.name: Harchand Singh Longowal
people.summary: Akali Dal president who signed the Punjab Accord with Rajiv Gandhi (July 1985) and was assassinated weeks later (NCERT).
facts: Akali Dal president from 1980 (NCERT).
Signed the Rajiv–Longowal Accord (24 July 1985) (NCERT).
Assassinated on 20 August 1985 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: Prafulla Kumar Mahanta
people.summary: AASU leader who signed the Assam Accord (1985) and became Chief Minister at 33 as head of the Asom Gana Parishad (NCERT).
facts: Led the Assam movement (1979–85) (NCERT).
AGP came to power in 1985 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: Laldenga
people.summary: Mizo National Front leader who led an armed revolt from 1966 and signed the Mizo Accord with Rajiv Gandhi (1986), becoming Chief Minister (NCERT).
facts: Led the MNF's armed campaign (1966) (NCERT).
Signed the peace accord (1986); Mizoram became a state (1987) (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

people.name: J.R. Jayewardene
people.summary: President of Sri Lanka who signed the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord with Rajiv Gandhi (29 July 1987).
facts: Signed the accord in Colombo; IPKF sent to Sri Lanka.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Department of Defense. American Forces Information Service. Defense Visual Information Center. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: V.P. Singh
people.summary: Prime Minister of the National Front government (1989–90) who decided to implement the Mandal Commission's OBC reservation (NCERT).
facts: Left the Congress over the Bofors issue; formed the Janata Dal (1988).
PM from 2 December 1989 with outside support from the BJP and the Left (NCERT).
Announced 27% OBC reservation in central jobs (August 1990) (NCERT).
Lost a confidence vote (November 1990).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howEnded: Lost a confidence vote after the BJP withdrew support

images.credit: Christian Lambiotte - European Commission / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: B.P. Mandal
people.summary: Chaired the Second Backward Classes Commission (1979–80), which recommended 27% reservation for OBCs (NCERT).
facts: Chief Minister of Bihar for about a month and a half in 1968 (NCERT).
His commission's report came in 1980 (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

people.name: Chandra Shekhar Singh
people.summary: Prime Minister (November 1990 – June 1991) with Congress support; under him India pledged gold to meet the balance-of-payments crisis.
facts: "Young Turk" of the Congress; walked across India (Bharat Yatra, 1983).
PM with outside Congress support; resigned in March 1991.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Manmohan Singh
people.summary: Economist who as Finance Minister (1991) launched the reforms and as Prime Minister (2004–14) led the UPA (NCERT).
facts: RBI Governor (1982–85).
Finance Minister under P.V. Narasimha Rao; presented the 24 July 1991 budget.
PM 2004–14; apologised in Parliament (2005) for the 1984 anti-Sikh violence (NCERT).
Indo-US nuclear deal (2008) (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howGained: Chosen by Sonia Gandhi after the UPA won (2004)

people.name: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
people.summary: "Missile Man of India": led SLV-3 (1980) and the missile programme, co-led Pokhran-II, and was President 2002–07.
facts: Project director of SLV-3, which put Rohini in orbit (18 July 1980).
Led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (1983): Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul, Nag.
Scientific Adviser during Pokhran-II (1998).
President 2002–07; Bharat Ratna 1997.
Wrote "Wings of Fire".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Y.V. Chandrachud
people.summary: Longest-serving Chief Justice of India (1978–85); led the benches in Minerva Mills (1980) and Shah Bano (1985).
facts: CJI for over seven years.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: V. Prabhakaran
people.summary: Leader of the LTTE, which fought the IPKF and assassinated Rajiv Gandhi (1991).
facts: Founded the LTTE (1976).
Killed by the Sri Lankan army (2009).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kanshi Ram
people.summary: Founder of BAMCEF (1978) and the Bahujan Samaj Party (1984) (NCERT).
facts: Left a government job for social work; founded BAMCEF, DS-4 and the BSP (NCERT).
Regarded political power as the master key to social equality (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

people.name: Giani Zail Singh
people.summary: First Sikh President of India (1982–87), in office during Operation Blue Star and Indira Gandhi's assassination.
facts: Swore in Rajiv Gandhi as PM (31 October 1984).
Used the pocket veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill (1986).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: H.D. Deve Gowda
people.summary: Janata Dal leader from Karnataka; Prime Minister of the United Front government (1996–97) (NCERT).
facts: Chief Minister of Karnataka before becoming PM (June 1996).
Lost office when the Congress withdrew support (April 1997).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

people.name: I.K. Gujral
people.summary: Prime Minister of the United Front (1997–98), known for the "Gujral Doctrine" of generous ties with neighbours.
facts: External Affairs Minister (1989–90, 1996–97).
Gujral Doctrine: help smaller neighbours without asking for reciprocity.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: N. Chandrababu Naidu
people.summary: TDP leader; CM of united Andhra Pradesh (1995–2004) known for IT-led development, and the first CM of residual Andhra Pradesh (2014).
facts: Took over the TDP and the CM's post from his father-in-law NTR (1 September 1995).
Convener of the United Front (1996); backed the NDA (1998–2004).
"Vision 2020"; HITEC City, Hyderabad (1998); Janmabhoomi programme.
Sworn in as CM of residual AP on 8 June 2014; chose Amaravati as capital.

roles.title: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh
roles.howGained: Won the support of most TDP MLAs against NTR (1995)

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy
people.summary: Congress CM of Andhra Pradesh (2004–09) known for welfare schemes; died in a helicopter crash on 2 September 2009.
facts: Praja Prasthanam padayatra of about 1,500 km in 2003.
Free power to farmers; Jalayagnam irrigation programme; Rajiv Arogyasri health insurance (2007); fee reimbursement.
Re-elected in 2009; killed in a helicopter crash in the Nallamala forest (2 September 2009).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: K. Rosaiah
people.summary: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh after YSR's death (September 2009 – November 2010).
facts: Long-serving Finance Minister of AP (presented 15 budgets).
Later Governor of Tamil Nadu.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: N. Kiran Kumar Reddy
people.summary: Last Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh (2010–14); resigned on 19 February 2014 in protest against bifurcation.
facts: Former Speaker; CM from 25 November 2010.
Opposed the bifurcation bill; resigned when it passed the Lok Sabha.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: K. Chandrasekhar Rao
people.summary: Founder of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi (27 April 2001) whose fast in November 2009 forced the Centre to start the process for Telangana; first CM of Telangana (2014).
facts: Resigned as Deputy Speaker and from the TDP to found the TRS (2001).
Union Labour Minister (2004–06) in the UPA.
Fast-unto-death from 29 November 2009 led to the 9 December announcement.
First CM of Telangana from 2 June 2014.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Digital Media Telangana Government / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Narendra Modi
people.summary: Chief Minister of Gujarat (2001–14), declared BJP's PM candidate in September 2013, and Prime Minister from 26 May 2014 after the BJP won a clear majority on its own (NCERT).
facts: CM of Gujarat 2001–14.
BJP's PM candidate (September 2013) (NCERT).
BJP won 282 seats in 2014 — the first single-party majority since 1984 (NCERT).
Launched Jan Dhan Yojana and Swachh Bharat (2014); laid the Amaravati foundation (2015).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 8 "Recent Developments in Indian Politics"

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howGained: BJP majority in the 16th Lok Sabha (NCERT)

people.name: Nawaz Sharif
people.summary: Prime Minister of Pakistan who signed the Lahore Declaration with Vajpayee (February 1999); overthrown by Musharraf (October 1999).
facts: Received Vajpayee on the Delhi–Lahore bus (February 1999).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pervez Musharraf
people.summary: Pakistani army chief who planned the Kargil intrusion (1999), seized power that October and met Vajpayee at Agra (2001).
facts: Army chief during Kargil.
Military coup (12 October 1999).
Agra Summit with Vajpayee (July 2001).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vikram Batra
people.summary: Captain who captured Point 5140 and died on Point 4875 in the Kargil war; Param Vir Chakra ("Yeh dil maange more").
facts: Param Vir Chakra (posthumous).
Called "Sher Shah" by the enemy.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: R. Chidambaram
people.summary: Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission who led Pokhran-II (1998) with Abdul Kalam.
facts: Involved in both Pokhran-I (1974) and Pokhran-II (1998).
Principal Scientific Adviser (2001–18).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: World Economic Forum from Cologny, Switzerland / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: P. Chidambaram
people.summary: Union Home Minister who announced on 9 December 2009 that the process of forming Telangana would begin.
facts: Home Minister after the 26/11 attacks (from 30 November 2008).
Finance Minister in several governments.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: B.N. Srikrishna
people.summary: Retired Supreme Court judge who headed the Committee for Consultations on the Situation in Andhra Pradesh (2010), which gave six options.
facts: Committee set up 3 February 2010; report 30 December 2010.
Also headed the inquiry into the 1992–93 Bombay riots.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: J.S. Verma
people.summary: Chief Justice who laid down the Vishaka guidelines (1997); later headed the Verma Committee on criminal law (2013).
facts: Vishaka judgment (1997).
Verma Committee after the December 2012 Delhi case.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Aruna Roy
people.summary: Founder of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (1990) whose Rajasthan campaign led to the Right to Information Act (2005).
facts: Left the IAS (1975).
MKSS jan sunwais (public hearings) on records in Rajasthan.
Ramon Magsaysay Award (2000).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sonia Gandhi
people.summary: Congress president (1998–2017) who led the UPA to power in 2004 and chose Manmohan Singh as PM.
facts: Declined the post of PM (May 2004).
Chairperson of the UPA and of the National Advisory Council.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: U.S. Department of State / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Anna Hazare
people.summary: Gandhian social worker from Ralegan Siddhi whose fasts in 2011 drove the demand for a Jan Lokpal.
facts: Fasted at Jantar Mantar (April 2011) and Ramlila Maidan (August 2011).
Led the RTI campaign in Maharashtra.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pranab Mukherjee
people.summary: President of India (2012–17) who gave assent to the AP Reorganisation Act (1 March 2014).
facts: Finance, Defence and External Affairs Minister in Congress governments.
President 2012–17; Bharat Ratna 2019.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: E.S.L. Narasimhan
people.summary: Governor of united Andhra Pradesh (2009–14) and then the common Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana (2014–19).
facts: Former Intelligence Bureau director.
Swore in KCR (2 June 2014) and Chandrababu Naidu (8 June 2014).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: K.C. Sivaramakrishnan
people.summary: Headed the expert committee under Section 6 of the AP Reorganisation Act on the new capital (report August 2014).
facts: Advised a decentralised capital and warned against using fertile delta land.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
